content:
- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.5) — reduce initial forecast by 1–2% for positive sentiment.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.2) — add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for bearish bias.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >70) — cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 70, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until price stabilizes.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was high 2–3 days prior, adjust forecast downward by 0.3–0.7% to account for delayed market reaction.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate volatility — reduce final 5–7 days of forecast by 0.5–1.0% to reflect diminishing momentum.
